title: fix(plugin-audit): an activity summary written right after a language change stores the new language
body:
Fixes #24235

Clause-②: no

The activity summary writer in `plugin-audit` held the workspace locale for each tenant/user scope for a flat 30 s. Nothing retired it when `localization.locale` changed, and a `sys_activity.summary` line is stored once, at write time. So every audited write made in the 30 s after a language change stored the old language permanently. This PR retires the held locale when either settings store is written through the engine. The 30 s TTL stays only as the bound for what that seam cannot see.

Responsibility: `plugin-audit`'s own writer (`resolveWriteLocale`'s TTL-only `localeCache`) | the platform path is the core resolver's success cache, retired by the settings generation and the engine write epoch, which the writer's memo sat above and outlived | reached by any workspace that changes `localization.locale` through `PUT /api/settings/localization` and writes within 30 s.

## The defect, measured before the fix

A one-off rig (a scratch file, deleted, never committed) at `main` `f5ef054a7`: `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` + the real `SettingsServicePlugin` + `AuditPlugin` over SQLite, with `Date` frozen.

| step | before (`f5ef054a7`) | after (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| audited write A, no setting yet | `Created Task "A"`, 2 settings reads | same |
| control: audited write B0, no change between | `Created Task "B0"`, **0** settings reads | same, **0** reads |
| `settings.set('localization', 'locale', 'zh-CN', tenant ctx)` | reads back `zh-CN`, source `tenant`; `resolveLocalizationContext` answers `zh-CN` | same |
| audited write B, right after the change | **`Created Task "B"`** (old language, stored for good) | **`创建了 Task "B"`** |
| audited write C, clock moved +31 s | `创建了 Task "C"` | same |

## The PM hypotheses, measured

- **Does the engine the audit plugin receives carry the write-epoch seam?** Yes. `ctx.getService('objectql')` is the `ObjectQL` instance (`objectql/src/plugin.ts` registers `this.ql`), and `writeEpoch.current` is a number on it. So the core resolver does cache a success there.
- **Can the settings branch read through the core resolver with no memo of its own?** It can, but its cache never hits for this caller. The engine bumps the epoch at the top of every insert, update and delete (`executeWithMiddleware`), and an audited write is one. By the time the writer's after-hook asks, the epoch has always moved. Measured on the same rig: two calls with no write between cost 2, then 0 settings reads; with one audited write between, the next call costs 2 again. Reading through, or retiring the writer's memo on the epoch itself, would add the full settings read (`sys_platform_setting` + `sys_setting`) to every audited write. The memo was written to keep that read off the hot path, and `memoizes the locale lookup per tenant/user scope (hot-path guard)` pins it. **So the suggested route was not taken.**
- **The route taken.** The writer keeps one memo and retires it with the writes that can change its answer. These are any `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` on `sys_setting` or `sys_platform_setting`, seen by the writer's own object-scoped hooks. `SettingsService` persists through this engine, so a change through the settings API is one of them. A direct row write, such as a seeder's, is the other, and it emits no settings event at all. These are the same writes that retire the core resolver's cache: its settings generation (the API path) and its epoch backstop (the direct path). One rule decides: an entry stamped with an older generation is dead. The generation is read before the lookup and stamped on its answer, as the core resolver stamps its epoch, so a settings write that lands while a lookup is in flight cannot leave the pre-write answer held.
- **The host branch** (`AuditPluginOptions.getLocale` via `createHostLocaleReader`) keeps the TTL-bounded memo. A host resolver offers no seam the writer can see, so the TTL is its only bound, as the card's Wanted says. A settings-store write also retires a held host answer. That costs one extra host call and changes no answer. Host-first precedence is unchanged: `audit-plugin.ts` is not touched.

## What changed

- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`: the memo entry carries the generation it was read at. `retireHeldLocales` advances the generation and is registered on the two settings objects for the three after-events, one string-scoped registration each. The handler re-checks `ctx.object`, because a dispatcher that ignored the scope would otherwise retire on every write. The `AuditWriterOptions.getLocale` doc now says when a held answer ends.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-write-locale-settings-seam.integration.test.ts` (new): the card's pin on a real engine. It uses `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` + `AuditPlugin`, SQLite, and a stand-in `sys_setting` under the real name; no settings service is registered, so the core resolver reads the store directly. `Date` is frozen, so nothing passes on the TTL. The case writes T1 in English and then a control write T2 with **0** `sys_setting` reads. An insert into `sys_setting` follows, and the next write stores `创建了 Task "T3"`. An update follows, and the next write stores `Task「T4」を作成しました`. A last unchanged write is held again, with 0 reads.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.test.ts`: two writer cases for what the real-engine pin cannot reach. The first covers each store, including `sys_platform_setting`, the global rung, with the no-write control. The second covers a settings write landing while a lookup is in flight.
- `.changeset/24235-audit-write-locale-seam.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit`.

## Contract (Clause-② measured)

The built `dist/index.d.ts` of `@objectstack/plugin-audit` was built at `f5ef054a7` and at this branch and then diffed. The only hunk is the JSDoc of `AuditWriterOptions.getLocale`, lines 234–237. No type, signature, export, option key or schema moves. `installAuditWriters`' options type and `AuditPluginOptions` keep their shape.

## Tests and gates (head `dc1de5306`, after merging `origin/main` `8eccf519d`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 56 files, **894 passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck`: exit 0. The test layer compiles both edited test files; `--listFiles` names them.
- **Ablation** (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, on the committed fix at `98e0d9fec`): the anchor is `hit.generation === generation &&`, dropped from the read check, which restores the old TTL-only memo. The anchor went x1 to x0 and the blob `f8bbd5f1b148` became `853a4ed4a906`. **3 red, 100 green**: the real-engine pin received `Created Task "T3"` and expected `创建了 Task "T3"`, and both writer cases went red. The restore was proven: blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **A second ablation, with a finding of its own.** The first version also carried a map clear and a store guard. Dropping the store guard alone stayed **green**, because the read check alone already decides. Both extra guards were removed (`98e0d9fec`), leaving the one rule the ablation above turns red.
- The derived gate list (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 68 commands) was run at this head: **68 of 68 exit 0**. That list is identical to the seat's lead at `f5ef054a7`, and `--ran` reconciles it as 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN, a derived zero because every line records its exit code. Among the verdict lines: `check-i18n-bundles: OK (10 package(s) — all bundles in sync`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads — 111 published require entry point(s) across 69 package(s) load`, `check-engine-double-contract: OK — 1022 pinned`, `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 12130 text file(s)` and `check-test-source-alias OK`. On the pre-merge head `98e0d9fec`, `check:i18n` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) because their build closure was missing. They passed once the gate's own prerequisite build ran, and both were re-run at `dc1de5306` above. Repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint`) and `test:repo` belong to CI; this diff touches no `test:repo` file.

## Acceptance notes

- **Two comments in `packages/core` describe the old staleness as harmless.** `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:1795`–`:1798` says that for the audit writer "a stale locale in a log line for up to 30s costs nothing observable". `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.test.ts:422`–`:428` makes the same point ("audit-writer's staleness tolerance"). A summary line is stored once, so the staleness was observable. Both comments also call the writer's memo a TTL-only cache, which is no longer true. `packages/core` is excluded from this card. Carrier: the `domain:engine` seat.
- **What the seam does not see.** Two cases stay bounded by the 30 s TTL. The first is a `localization` write on another node: the core resolver gets a remote epoch bump through the `authz.invalidated` bridge, and this writer does not subscribe to the epoch. The second is the storage behind a host `getLocale` resolver. A `SettingsService` with no engine bound writes nothing the writer can see, but no stock composition reaches that: the service refuses writes until it is bound (`engineBindPending`), and the audit writer is not installed without an engine.
- **Retirement is coarse.** Any write to either settings store retires every held locale, whatever its namespace. A predicate update names no namespace the hook can read without fetching the row. Settings writes are rare, so the cost is one locale read per scope.
